**v1.14.4: the bot runs Wizard101 at High priority, so the freeze when a menu, card or enchant loads for the first time in a while is shorter.**

- **New: "Run Wizard101 at High priority" (Settings, on by default).**
  - **Why:** Wizard101 freezes for a moment when it opens the spellbook, the backpack, a card or an enchant (Sharpen, damage boosts) it hasn't shown for a few minutes. It builds that menu there and then, on the thread that draws the game. Its own log shows "TIMING Event DisplayCharStats took 138 ms" when opening the spellbook. This happens on every PC, and no game setting changes it. With the game set to High priority in Task Manager, the freezes were much shorter (2026-11-18). They're shorter, not gone.
  - **What it does:** each Wizard101 the bot sees is set to High priority once. That includes both games in carry mode and a game hidden in the tray. It's the same as Task Manager's Details tab, Set priority, High. The bot checks that it worked, and debug.log says "Wizard101 (pid N) at High priority now". It's never Realtime.
  - **Your own choice:** if you change the game's priority by hand afterwards, the bot leaves it alone while it runs. A restart of the bot sets High again, so switch the option off to keep your own. Switching it off puts the games it raised back to Normal.
- **Checked:** the new code ran against stand-in processes, not the game, and passed 23 of 23 checks: raising each game once, switching off and on, and new games. A new test file pins the setting and the code, the five release scripts load, and 856 of 895 vision tests pass (38 are skipped on this PC). `test_ahk_names`' speedhack path test errors, as on v1.12.0. Not tried in the game yet.
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install. Your settings, learned cards, routes and recorded battles are kept. The new option is on after the update. A copy run from the code: git pull.
